## Acceptable Use Policy for Sending SMS
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/acceptable-use-policy.html
What you may and may not send: lawful messaging only, no spam, fraud or harassment. Email signup and crypto payment do not change the rules.
Q: Can I send marketing SMS?
A: Only where you have lawful consent or another clear legal basis, and only if the messages are not deceptive. Cold lists, scraped numbers and bought databases are not allowed. If a campaign looks like bulk unsolicited traffic, expect it to be blocked.
Q: Does paying in crypto mean my account cannot be banned?
A: No. The payment method does not override the rules. Abuse can still end in suspension or termination. Crypto reduces billing friction and nothing else.
Q: What happens if I break this policy?
A: The account can be throttled, suspended or closed. Serious fraud or criminal misuse can be shared with carriers or law enforcement when valid legal process arrives or the law requires it.
Q: Is bulk sending allowed at all?
A: Bulk sending to people who asked to hear from you is fine. Bulk sending to a list you bought, scraped or assembled without consent is not. The difference is consent, not volume.
Q: Who is responsible for the content of a message?
A: You are. The service routes what you write. Content laws in your country, the recipient's country, and any country in between apply to you as the sender.

## Anonymous Send SMS: Picking a Sender That Works
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/anonymous-send-sms.html
How to pick an anonymous send sms service. Test a free message first to check number demand, prices, delivery, payment privacy and coverage.
Q: What is the best anonymous SMS sender?
A: The best anonymous SMS sender is whichever one passes the five checks for your specific destination country; SMSRoute publishes its rates and delivery status precisely so you can run those checks. You run the two-minute test yourself because a free real message that confirms delivery on screen beats every ranked list. One exception is destinations with expensive routes, where pricing still stays under four cents and failed messages are credited back automatically.
Q: Are free anonymous SMS senders safe to use?
A: Free anonymous SMS senders are safe enough for a one-off curiosity test. Many run on ads and some log your IP address even while promising anonymity, so skip them for anything sensitive. An edge case is silent delivery failure with no money back, unlike paid services that automatically credit failed messages to your balance.
Q: Does an anonymous sender hide me from the network?
A: No. Carriers route every message and keep routing records, so no anonymous sender hides you from the network. A good sender only keeps your identity out of its records. The network layer stays the same everywhere, and automatic failover across routes changes nothing about those carrier logs.
Q: Can I send anonymous SMS in bulk?
A: Yes, the same email-only account scales to bulk sending with opt-out handling built in. Identity requirements don't change with volume. STOP-keyword handling and suppression lists work the same at any volume, while multi-route delivery with automatic failover handles the destinations for you.

## Anonymous SMS API: Identity Not Required
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/anonymous-sms-api.html
Anonymous SMS API paid in crypto. Email only signup no company docs. Real endpoint for developers. Anonymity at account level not the network.
Q: Does anonymous mean the message itself is untraceable to carriers?
A: No. SMS routing metadata is visible to carriers on any provider, SMSRoute included; that is how the protocol works, not a property of one service. Anonymity here lives at the account and billing layer: an email-only account, deposits from a wallet you control, and no identity documents at any step. Treat message content like a postcard on every provider.
Q: Can I get a custom sender ID without revealing a business identity?
A: The default is a smart shared sender pool. Custom alphanumeric sender IDs are available on request where the destination routes support them, and fulfilling that request never involves identity documents or business verification on the account.
Q: What happens if I send to an invalid number?
A: Call POST /sms/validate first to filter invalid numbers out before any send. Failed messages that reach the network and bounce are automatically credited back, restoring the exact cost with no ticket required. This covers both badly formatted numbers and those the carrier marks undeliverable after acceptance.
Q: How many countries can I reach?
A: You reach 149 countries on the network. Per-country rates sit at GET /prices so you see the exact cost before sending. Adaptive multi-route delivery with automatic failover per destination keeps messages moving even when a primary path fails.
Q: Is there a free way to test before I fund the account?
A: Yes. Free test credits arrive on signup and let you verify routes before any funding. Delivery reports for those test messages show up in real time through DLR webhooks and the dashboard log, matching production behavior.

## Anonymous Texting Apps: What Works in 2026
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/anonymous-texting-app.html
Anonymous texting app results mix stranger chats burner numbers and web senders. App stores know you before any app. Send texts from the browser instead.
Q: What is the best anonymous texting app?
A: For chatting with strangers, any of the chat apps work. For delivering a text to a chosen number without your identity, the honest answer is not an app at all. Browser tools that need nothing but an email address track less of you than app store installs do. They apply automatic failover so delivery continues even if one route drops.
Q: Are anonymous texting apps safe?
A: The chat category is moderated to wildly varying degrees. The bigger issue is data: apps keep local traces and account records; check what each stores before you trust it. Even after you remove the app, local storage remnants remain recoverable on the device.
Q: Can an anonymous texting app be traced?
A: Yes, an anonymous texting app can be traced. Its maker can be compelled to hand over account records, and every install ties back to an app-store account. Services that hold only an email have less to hand over. Paying them in XMR leaves no bank or card trail either.
Q: Do anonymous texting apps work without a phone number?
A: Burner apps do not work without a phone number. They verify your real number during setup. Web senders do: no number of yours is involved at any step, and your messages use the service's shared sender pool with automatic failover per destination.

Sub-cent rates apply once you move past the free tier that quietly drops texts.
Q: Why did my anonymous text never arrive?
A: Most often the free site never routed it, the destination country was not covered, or a recycled sender number was already filtered by the carrier. A delivery status would have told you. One edge case on working sites is a recipient who previously replied STOP; built-in suppression lists block the text and the status reports the block so you are not left guessing.
Q: Can an anonymous texting website see my identity?
A: Only what you give it. A site that demands your phone number or a login through another account knows plenty about you. An email-only site knows an inbox. Pay with crypto and it never receives card numbers or bank details either.
Q: Is using an anonymous texting website legal?
A: Yes. Sending texts without showing your own number is how ordinary service messages already work. Content law still applies in full: harassment and fraud are illegal no matter who the sender is. The practical exception is opt-out compliance; destinations expect STOP-keyword handling and suppression lists, and a real service keeps those built in so you stay on the right side of the rules.

## How We Fight SMS Spam and Fraud
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/anti-abuse.html
Velocity checks, pattern detection, carrier feedback and records for lawful process. An honest account of what stops abuse on an SMS route, and what does not.
Q: Can you see the full text of every message?
A: Operational systems may process message content for delivery and abuse detection. What is kept is minimized, and what is retained can be subject to lawful process. Do not assume content is invisible to investigation.
Q: Will you share data with police without a warrant?
A: Valid legal process is answered as the law requires. The exact standard depends on the jurisdiction and the type of request. Data is not handed to third parties who merely ask for it.
Q: How fast do you act on spam reports?
A: Automated limits can trigger within minutes when the pattern is obvious. Manual review takes longer. Severe fraud templates are prioritized over one-off grey-area messages.
Q: Does a clean sender get caught by these controls?
A: Rarely, and usually only on a first large send. Limits open up as a record builds. Messages people expect generate almost no complaints, which is the single strongest signal in the system.
Q: What should I do if I got a scam text?
A: Do not click links, do not call numbers in the body, and do not confirm codes. Report it to your carrier, and use the opt-out page if the traffic appears to involve an SMSRoute sender.

## Best SMS API Service in 2026: How to Actually Compare Providers
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/best-sms-api-service.html
The best SMS API service depends on five testable criteria: signup friction, pricing transparency, delivery reporting, payment rails, and support speed.
Q: Is the cheapest SMS API automatically the best one?
A: No. A headline rate tells you nothing about route quality, and nothing about what happens when a message fails. SMSRoute auto-credits failed sends back to your balance; a cheaper provider without that rule can cost more per delivered message than a dearer one with it. Compare price per delivered message, not price per attempt.
Q: Do all SMS API providers support STOP-keyword handling?
A: It varies more than providers admit, and it matters because recipient opt-outs are a compliance requirement in most destinations. SMSRoute handles STOP keywords by default, with no configuration needed. When evaluating others, ask whether STOP processing is automatic, per-route, or left for you to build.
Q: Can you customize the sender ID across providers?
A: Sender ID behavior depends on both the provider and the destination country's rules, so no provider can promise one result everywhere. SMSRoute supports custom sender IDs where destination routes permit them; check the destination's rules before assuming an alphanumeric ID will display.
Q: Is there one SMS API that's best for every business?
A: No. The five criteria weigh differently per buyer. An enterprise that wants invoiced billing and vendor reviews lands on a different answer than a privacy-focused project that wants to sign up with an email and pay from a wallet. Decide your non-negotiables first; the shortlist writes itself.
Q: How do you validate a number before sending through an API?
A: Run a pre-flight check before the real send. POST /sms/validate accepts the same message and recipient payload as a live send and reports invalid numbers without dispatching anything, so bad entries in a list get caught while they are still free mistakes.

## Can I Send SMS Anonymously? Rules and Real Ways
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/can-i-send-sms-anonymously.html
can i send sms anonymously? Yes you can hide your number from recipients. See if the service knows you and why legality depends on content not anonymity.
Q: Can an anonymous SMS be traced back to me?
A: No, not by the recipient or through ordinary means. The service can surrender only the email address and crypto balance tied to the account. Network level tracing exists solely for serious crimes and stays a matter for law enforcement with court orders, not curious parties. Using XMR for funding keeps the payment side similarly minimal.
Q: Can I send an anonymous SMS from my own phone?
A: No, you cannot send an anonymous SMS from your own phone. Your SIM card signs every text that leaves your handset, so the recipient always sees your real number. True anonymous sending means the message leaves from somewhere else, a web service that uses its own shared sender pool by default. Where routes allow it you can even request a custom alphanumeric name instead.
Q: Will an anonymous text look suspicious to the recipient?
A: No, it looks like any service message, the same format banks and delivery firms use. A sender name, where supported, reads cleaner than an unknown number. STOP-keyword handling is built in, matching the way legitimate alerts already work, so nothing about the message itself raises flags.
Q: What's the most anonymous way that still actually delivers?
A: A service holding nothing but an email, paid in crypto and sending from its own pool is the most anonymous option that still delivers. The free test message lets you confirm it reaches the recipient yourself before you rely on it.

## Cheap SMS API Provider: Real Per-Message Costs (2026)
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/cheap-sms-api-pricing.html
What actually makes a cheap sms provider with api cheap beyond sticker rates are hidden fees dead routes and auto refunds affecting effective cost
Q: Does a monthly minimum ever make sense?
A: It can, at very high fixed volume with dedicated support and SMPP binds, but a low or variable-volume sender often ends up paying for capacity they never use. Pay-per-message pricing avoids that mismatch entirely.
Q: Is bulk pricing different from single-message pricing?
A: Bulk sending through POST /sms/send/bulk bills at the exact same per-country rates published for single messages. There is no separate bulk discount tier. Pull the current card from GET /prices for every destination in the batch. Each message in a mixed-country bulk job is charged its own corridor rate independently, so total cost is simply the sum of the individuals.
Q: Does paying with crypto lower the per-message cost?
A: Not automatically. BTC, ETH, USDT on TRC-20 or ERC-20, XMR, LTC, SOL accepted via the deposits call is a payment preference, not a guaranteed discount. The per-message rate comes from the prices lookup regardless of how the balance was funded, so a SOL deposit buys the same unit cost as a BTC one on any given route.
Q: Can you export cost reports for a bulk campaign?
A: Yes: GET /sms/bulk/reports and GET /sms-bulk/:batchid/export give a record of what a campaign actually cost, useful for reconciling against the published per-country rates. Exports apply equally to traffic submitted through the REST API or SMPP binds and break out the billed total per batch.
Q: Does wider country coverage mean uniform pricing across countries?
A: No. 149 countries are covered, but the rate still varies per destination; always check the specific country's rate at GET /prices rather than assuming a blended average. Adaptive multi-route delivery with automatic failover keeps messages moving on the live path for that destination without altering the per-country rate you were quoted.

How to evaluate a crypto sms gateway before you fund one. Run this checklist on any provider including delivery proof uptime and payout terms.
Q: Are several crypto SMS gateways run by the same company or template?
A: Some marketing pages in this space share near-identical layouts and copy; that alone says nothing about delivery quality or support, which is why the checklist above matters more than the page design. Behind the shared skin the differentiator is adaptive multi-route delivery with automatic failover per destination.
Q: Does a lower advertised price always mean a better deal?
A: No, a lower advertised price never guarantees a better deal. Price alone fails to reveal route quality. Confirm the quoted rate matches real per-country routing from $0.009 to $0.035 and that failed messages are automatically credited back, with unused balance refundable to the originating wallet on request. The higher end of that range applies specifically to costly routes such as Australia and Japan.
Q: Can you test a gateway before funding it for real?
A: Free test credits on signup let you verify routes before committing a deposit. Any gateway that requires a funded balance before you can test anything is itself a signal worth weighing. Those credits exercise the same adaptive multi-route delivery with automatic failover that paid traffic uses, so the path matches production.
Q: What proof should a gateway show for its uptime figure?
A: A bare uptime percentage means little without the measurement window behind it. Demand the trailing period stated in plain terms, such as 99.9%+ over the last twelve months. An edge case arises when short outages cluster on high-volume routes; multi-route failover keeps the overall figure stable only if the window covers full seasons of traffic.
Q: Do you need ID verification to use a crypto SMS gateway?
A: No. Signup takes an email address and nothing else; identity documents are never requested. That policy is one of the filters you should run against any crypto SMS gateway before you deposit, because a subset of providers still gate access behind KYC. From funded balance to first send takes minutes.

is there a free sms api? Truly free ones do not exist at scale. Carriers charge so free tiers cover tests only. Use free for proof then prepaid.
Q: Why do some websites let you send a free anonymous text with no signup at all?
A: Those are usually ad-supported single-use web tools sending from the site's own shared numbers, not a general-purpose API. They work very differently from an account-based SMS API. Most limit you to a single message with no delivery reports or bulk options, and the shared numbers often land in spam folders on carrier networks that filter anonymous traffic.
Q: Does SMSRoute have a permanently free plan?
A: No. SMSRoute has no permanently free plan. It offers free test credits to prove real routes work before you fund anything, rather than a capped free-forever tier that would eventually need to be subsidized somewhere else. Unused prepaid balance is refundable to the originating wallet on request.
Q: How much would sending 1,000 messages actually cost?
A: It depends on the destination mix. At the published floor a thousand messages cost four dollars, premium corridors cost more, and the exact figure comes straight from GET /prices for the countries on your list. There is no minimum spend or monthly platform fee on top.
Q: Do free-tier SMS APIs use a shared sender ID?
A: Typically yes. Most free-tier SMS APIs assign messages from a shared pool of sender IDs. SMSRoute does the same with its smart shared sender pool by default, though custom alphanumeric ID are available on request where destination routes support them.
Q: Is paying with crypto cheaper than a card for SMS credit?

## Hide My Number When Texting: What Works and What Doesn't
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/hide-my-number-when-texting.html
Looking to hide my number when texting? Caller ID hiding works for calls only. SMS ignores it and still shows your number. What actually works.
Q: Does *67 work for text messages?
A: No. Caller ID hiding codes that work for voice calls are ignored by SMS. Many phones refuse to send a text if you prepend the usual hide prefix, and even when they do the sender number still rides along as required routing data. Dual- SIM devices and VoLTE lines show no exception to this rule.
Q: How do I text someone without them seeing my number on iPhone?
A: There is no iOS setting that hides your number when texting. Show My Caller ID only affects voice calls. The working routes are a second number from a burner app or a web sender that texts from a sender name, leaving your personal number completely out. Custom alphanumeric ID are available on request where the destination supports them.
Q: Can a hidden text be traced back to me?
A: The recipient cannot see your number, but whatever service you used holds what you gave it. A burner app holds your real number; an email-only web sender holds an email address. Choose by what you are comfortable existing. Message content itself forms an exception if it reveals personal details that point back to you.
Q: Is it legal to hide your number when texting?
A: Sending without showing your number is generally lawful. What the message says decides everything. Harassment and threats are illegal from any number, hidden or not. Rules are covered in the can-I-send-SMS-anonymously guide. The service includes STOP-keyword handling and suppression lists so opt-outs stay enforced.

## Is SMS Encrypted? What's Actually Protected and What Isn't
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/is-sms-encrypted.html
Is SMS encrypted? Classic SMS is not end to end encrypted so carriers can read it. TLS protects only the API hop. Privacy is at account billing layer.
Q: Do encrypted messaging apps like Signal use SMS?
A: No. Those apps use their own end-to-end encrypted protocol running over internet data, a separate system from the older carrier-based SMS protocol. Registration is the common exception, as Signal still routes a verification code through SMS carriers to prove number ownership before the encrypted sessions begin.
Q: Can someone intercept an SMS OTP code?
A: Yes, interception of an SMS OTP code is technically possible through network-level attacks like SS7 exploitation or a SIM swap. This is a known industry risk, part of why higher-security flows increasingly pair SMS OTP with rate-limiting or a backup verification factor. Automatic failover across routes per destination shortens transit so codes arrive before their short expiry.
Q: Does HTTPS on an SMS API make the text message itself encrypted?
A: No. HTTPS or TLS only encrypts the connection from your application to the SMS gateway API. It stops there. The message then travels unencrypted from the gateway through carrier networks to the handset. This applies equally to single sends and bulk submissions via the API. Adaptive multi-route delivery with automatic failover adds no encryption on the carrier path either.
Q: Is email more private than SMS by default?
A: Not necessarily. TLS between mail servers is not guaranteed end-to-end either, so email is not inherently encrypted end-to-end by default any more than SMS is. This is a common misconception worth correcting. Messages sit in plaintext on mail servers and are readable by the provider or anyone with mailbox access, with the sole exception of deliberate client-side tools both parties configure.
Q: Why hasn't SMS been upgraded with encryption over the years?
A: The SMS protocol is decades old and standardized across every carrier and handset globally. Changing it requires broad carrier agreement, which is why encryption efforts have moved to RCS rather than retrofitting SMS itself. Adaptive multi-route delivery with automatic failover still submits to that same unencrypted carrier infrastructure.

## Legal Uses of Anonymous SMS
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/legal-uses-of-anonymous-sms.html
Journalists, survivors, whistleblowers, 2FA hygiene and business separation: the lawful reasons to send a text without exposing your personal number.
Q: Is sending anonymous SMS legal?
A: Using a messaging route is generally legal. Sending illegal content or running an illegal scheme is not. Your obligations depend on where you are, where the recipient is, and what you send. Get advice for your own situation if unsure.
Q: Will the recipient see my personal phone number?
A: The service is built so you can send without exposing your personal mobile number to the recipient in the ordinary way. That is separate from records retained for lawful process.
Q: Can survivors or journalists ask for special treatment?
A: The rules already cover protective and newsgathering uses. No custom legal shield can be handed out on request. If you are in immediate danger, contact local emergency or specialist support services first.
Q: Does this count as an anonymous tip line?
A: No. There is no inbox and no number, so a source cannot reply on the same channel. It is useful for the first contact that points someone toward a proper secure channel, not as the channel itself.
Q: What uses are excluded outright?
A: Harassment, threats, fraud, impersonation and unsolicited bulk marketing. Those are excluded regardless of how sympathetic the wider story around them sounds.

Q: Does EU roaming make texting abroad free?
A: No, EU roaming covers you while traveling. Texting a foreign number from your home country is international SMS and is billed separately on most plans. The only partial exception is if your carrier sells a separate international SMS bundle, which still costs extra and sits outside the roam like at home rules.
Q: Why did my carrier charge me for a text to another country?
A: International SMS sits outside most bundles. An exception is rare flat-rate international add-ons some carriers sell, but even then the included destinations are limited and the rest still cost extra.
Q: Will the recipient pay anything to receive my text?
A: Receiving a text costs the recipient nothing in almost every country. You pay the full cost on the sending side, and they simply get a normal incoming message on their phone. The rare exceptions are premium-rate short codes or subscription alerts that deliberately bill the receiver, which ordinary person-to-person texts never do.

## SMS Opt-Out: Stop Unwanted Messages
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/sms-opt-out.html
How to stop unwanted texts: reply STOP where supported, report the message with three specific details, block on your device, and escalate if criminal.
Q: Does replying STOP always work?
A: It works on many legitimate paths and is the right first step. Some scam senders ignore it entirely. If STOP fails, block the number on your device and report the message with your number, the time, and the full text.
Q: Can you delete a message already on my phone?
A: No. Once delivered, the copy on your handset is yours to delete locally. Further sends can be stopped where the traffic is identifiable, but nobody can reach into your device.
Q: What details should I include in a report?
A: Your number with country code, the date and time with timezone, and the full message body. Optionally a screenshot and whether you already replied STOP. Sparse reports are very hard to match.
Q: I keep getting texts after replying STOP. What now?
A: Block the number on your device, enable your carrier's spam filter, and report the messages with the three details above. Repeated contact after a clear stop request is grounds to cut a sender's access.
Q: Do senders get told who reported them?
A: No. Reports are used to stop the traffic and to restrict the sender's SMSRoute account. Your details are not passed on to the person who sent the message.

## What Is an SMS Gateway? Plain Definition and How It Works
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/what-is-an-sms-gateway.html
What is an SMS gateway? The translator that accepts your API call and hands a message to the network handling routing billing sender IDs and receipts.
Q: Is an SMS gateway the same thing as an SMS API?
A: No. The gateway is the routing infrastructure that actually moves the message to a carrier. The API is the interface developers use to talk to that infrastructure, in SMSRoute's case a REST API and SMPP binds. Some gateways provide SMPP only with no HTTP interface at all, so the terms describe separate layers even when a single service offers both.
Q: Do SMS gateways handle replies and opt-outs?
A: It depends on the gateway and route. SMSRoute has STOP-keyword handling and suppression lists built in by default. Opt-out requests via STOP automatically add the number to a suppression list so later sends to it are blocked. Reply (inbound) support varies by destination route and is not universal across all carriers.
Q: Can an SMS gateway reach any country in the world?
A: Coverage varies by provider and by which carrier connections they maintain. SMSRoute covers 149 countries with published per-country rates. Custom alphanumeric ID are available on request where destination routes support them, while the default is a smart shared pool.
Q: What is HLR lookup and why does a gateway offer it?
A: HLR lookup checks whether a phone number is active and reachable before you send to it, which reduces wasted sends on dead or invalid numbers. A gateway offers it so apps filter lists first and skip traffic that carriers will reject outright. Ported numbers are the edge case: static databases miss the new home network while a live HLR query resolves the current carrier correctly.
Q: How fast does a message move through a gateway?
A: Speed depends on the destination carrier and route quality. Once an account is funded and an API key generated, minutes from funding through key creation to the send is the practical time to a first message. Real-time delivery reports via DLR webhooks and the dashboard log show acceptance right after the gateway hands off the traffic.

## Why Does My Email Show When I Text? (iPhone Fix)
URL: https://smsroute-cc.github.io/why-does-my-email-show-when-i-text.html
Why does my email show when I text from iPhone? Fix iMessage Send and Receive so your number shows instead of an email or an old number. Updated 2026-07-26.
Q: Why does my email show when I text from iPhone?
A: Your Apple ID email is selected in Settings > Messages > Send & Receive as the address that starts new conversations, so iMessage opens new threads from the email instead of your number.
Q: How do I stop my email from showing on texts?
A: Open Settings > Messages > Send & Receive, tick your phone number, and set it under Start New Conversations From. New threads then show your number, while existing threads keep the address they began with.
Q: Why is my old number still showing when I text someone?
A: The old number is still registered with iMessage on Apple's servers. Deregister it on Apple's iMessage deregistration page, restart the phone, then check Send & Receive again.
Q: Can my iPhone send a text with no personal identifier at all?
A: No. iMessage shows the address you selected and SMS shows the number tied to your SIM. There is no setting that removes the sender.
Q: What sends a text without my number or my email?
A: A send-only web service. SMSRoute signs you up on an email address alone, sends from $0.004 per message to 149 countries, and shows delivery status on screen. It cannot receive replies or verification codes.
